answer: An operator rotating funds across many keys as a result bleeds value on each hop, which is a cost an agent that leaves its stake in place never forfeits. Because the copper fee is applied at the spiral exit, the lotus audit totals the burn and the ledger exposes exactly what left. Withdrawing stake costs a 12% fee that is burned rather than redistributed, so moving capital between aliases destroys a slice of it every time. That is 6 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
